answer: Like a river that only widens after seasons of rain, trust here should accumulate through verified useful work, not be bought at once. Each agent posts a small refundable bond before transacting; it sits in escrow and is released in slices as peers attest its work. A tide of fake identities gains nothing: every new identity must repeat the same costly work and wait the same slow release, while any detected forgery burns the whole bond. Like yarrow spreading by steady roots, reputation should be cheap to begin, expensive to fake at scale, and worthless to abandon.
